thread:
eva-ml: Heads up — nightly evals flagged a regression on the new q4 quantized build for redwood/open-7b. Exact_match down 6.3 pts, BLEU down 4.1. Threshold alarm fired. CI report: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/evals/6543 :eyes:

maria-p: ugh. Is this the quantization PR we merged yesterday?

devin-r: We merged a rounding tweak in q4 kernels (PR #4821) yesterday evening. It was small but touches async_kv and the matmul path for int8->fp16 ramp.

sam-s: Could be runtime kernel change, or the quantize mapping tables. Any repro on a single example?

eva-ml: I ran the eval runner locally against the failing suite. Repro is consistent. Pasted logs below.

```
$ python eval_runner.py --model redwood/open-7b-q4 --suite regression_suite_v2 --seed 42
Running 1200 examples
Metric summary: exact_match: 0.732 -> 0.669 (-0.063), bleu: 0.412 -> 0.371 (-0.041)
First failing example id=37
Model output: "Set the field to 'NONE'"
Expected:     "Set the field to 'None'"
```

kai-d: That diff (NONE vs None) smells like tokenization/normalization difference in the eval harness, not necessarily model semantics. Did the runner change normalization?
alex-oncall: CI job shows eval_runner v0.23.2 used yesterday; master is v0.23.3. The only change in v0.23.3 was a refactor around whitespace normalization in metrics.

ci-bot: build 6543 failed evals (regression_suite_v2) — failing rate 9.8% — logs attached.

devin-r: hmm. The quantization PR did change decoding-related fused-kernel config to improve perf; it's possible an off-by-one rounding in the kv cache index changed end-of-sequence tokens in edge cases. I'll bisect.

maria-p: If this blocks the release, we need a decision quickly. What's the impact on end-user quality?

eva-ml: For few-shot summarization tests we saw small differences but non-negligible -- some answers flip. For our regression suite the breaking examples are low-frequency tokens. Policy: any >3% EM regression flags release hold.

sam-s: I'll start a binary bisect across runtime commits yesterday. @devin-r can you run an eval-harness bisect too (runner vs kernel)?

devin-r: Starting bisect now. Running parallel evals across 6 commits. I'll update with the first positive/negative.

(30 minutes pass)

devin-r: Bisect update: commit range narrowed. Bad commit: 0a9f7c4 — "q4: change rounding behavior for matmul dequant". Reverting that commit locally fixes the suite.

sam-s: Confirmed revert in staging fixes kernels. But alex-oncall points out that eval_runner v0.23.3 normalization refactor also landed yesterday which could explain token case normalization. We need to be sure which change caused the metric drop.

alex-oncall: I ran the harness with master runtime + eval_runner@v0.23.2 -> no regression. runtime@0a9f7c4 + eval_runner@v0.23.2 -> regression reproduced. runtime@0a9f7c4 + eval_runner@v0.23.3 -> regression also reproduced. So culprit is runtime commit 0a9f7c4.

maria-p: So it's a runtime kernel rounding change. Is that safe to revert for the release? What's the perf impact if we revert?

devin-r: Reverting removes a micro-optimization that shaved ~4% token throughput in microbenchmarks. It shouldn't be customer-breaking. For safety, I'd prefer a revert and follow-up fix.

kai-d: One more note: I inspected the metric implementation and found a brittle normalization step in runner that uppercases the first char for certain outputs. That made EM sensitive to trailing punctuation changes. Filed #2345 to make eval metrics normalization deterministic. But current bisect points to runtime as root cause.

sam-s: Proposed plan: 1) revert runtime commit 0a9f7c4 in staging and prod rollback for dedicated pools, 2) block merge of next q4 releases until fix & regression test added, 3) open postmortem and assign owners for a proper kernel fix, 4) add CI gating: run regression_suite_v2 on merge of quantization kernel PRs.

maria-p: Agree. This is a release blocker; block the release until revert is live on dedicated. Notify customers?

devin-r: Creating revert PR now: #4850. Will tag @sam-s and @alex-oncall for review.

deploy-bot: Revert PR created: https://git.redwood/internal/pr/4850 by devin-r — CI will run full perf + eval matrix.

ci-bot: Triggering ad-hoc eval job for revert candidate. Job 6550 queued.

eva-ml: I'll add a new regression test that targets the edge tokens uncovered by the suite and add it to the mandatory gating list. Also will push the normalization fix for metrics in a separate PR to avoid future confusion.

maria-p: Thanks team. Please add an entry to incidents/ and postmortem once we finish the revert and root-cause. If revert hits any perf regressions, call it out.

alex-oncall: Note: if revert is fast and CI passes, we can un-block the release tomorrow morning. If CI fails, we hold and escalate.

sam-s: I'll run an isolated perf comparison on the revert branch and report numbers here.

(2 hours later)

devin-r: Revert PR merged to staging. ad-hoc eval job 6550 -> pass. Perf delta: -0.8% median token throughput vs previous micro-opt (within noise). Marking release unblocked pending prod deploy.

maria-p: Great work. Assigning owners: devin-r (runtime fix), eva-ml (regression tests + metric normalization), kai-d (CI gating). I'll draft a short customer note if prod deploy causes any user-visible change.

ci-bot: Prod deploy for revert scheduled at 2025-11-22T03:15Z (deploy id 7721) by sam-s.

end of thread: we'll follow up in postmortem.
